# CBDB-Desktop: Query Builder (QBE) revisions, 2026-10-20

Found while writing the Query Builder section of the user's guide, not from an automated-testing report, so these entries have no CBDB-D numbers yet. Assign numbers as needed. Changes are in qbe.html, qbe_gridstate.go, qbe_sqlgen.go, qbe_handlers.go and qbe_criteria.go. The Go changes were compiled, vetted and tested against stand-ins; the page script was syntax-checked and driven in a scripted browser (jsdom) against a mock server. Still to test in the running app.

## Summary

| Ref | Issue | Fix | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| QBE-1 | Table boxes had a fixed field-list height (up to 220px) | Field list starts at its natural height (max 220px) and can be resized by dragging its lower-right corner; join lines follow | Tested (jsdom) |
| QBE-2 | The workspace was a fixed 420px tall | Workspace can be resized vertically by dragging its lower-right corner (min 160px) | Tested |
| QBE-3 | The SQL tab showed ? placeholders instead of criteria values | Server returns a display copy of the SQL with values filled in as SQL literals; Copy SQL and Save SQL buttons added | Compiled, tested |
| QBE-4 | A join could link only one pair of fields | Join modal has "+ Add fields" for further pairs, AND'd into the same ON clause | Compiled, tested |
| QBE-5 | bindArg turned the criterion Nan (or Inf, Infinity) into a float NaN/Inf, which matched nothing | NaN and Inf are no longer accepted as numbers | Compiled, tested |

## QBE-1: Resizable table boxes

- .field-list now has resize: vertical and min-height: 24px in place of max-height: 220px.
- addTableBox() sets the list's initial height to its natural height, capped at 220px. An explicit height (not max-height) is what lets the user make it taller as well as shorter.
- A ResizeObserver on each box redraws its join lines when its height changes, since lines attach at the box's vertical midpoint. Observers are disconnected when a box is removed or Clear All is used.
- addTableBox() now switches to the Build the Query tab first. Previously, clicking a table while the Results or SQL tab was showing added a box the user couldn't see.

## QBE-2: Resizable workspace

- .qbe-canvas-wrap has resize: vertical and min-height: 160px; it still starts at 420px.
- .qbe-connectors (the SVG that draws join lines) now has overflow: visible, so lines to boxes dragged beyond the initially visible area are no longer clipped.
- The workspace height is not remembered between visits.

## QBE-3: Criteria values in the SQL tab

**Back end.** New InlineArgsForDisplay(query, args) in qbe_sqlgen.go replaces each ? outside quoted text with its bound value written as a SQL literal (sqlLiteral): integers bare, reals bare with a decimal point (1.0 stays REAL), text in single quotes with embedded ' doubled. qbeRunHandler returns this display copy in sql. **The query actually executed is still the parameterized one**, so criteria text still never becomes part of executed SQL.

If SQLite rejects the query, the response now also includes the SQL, so the SQL tab shows what failed.

Example (user's guide, first case):

WHERE "t2"."c_name_chn" = '蘇軾'

**Front end.** The SQL tab has **Copy SQL** (clipboard; falls back to selecting the text for Ctrl+C) and **Save SQL** (downloads QBEQuery.sql, UTF-8 without a BOM). Both are disabled until a query has been run, and after Clear All. downloadTextFile() gained an optional withBOM argument (default true, so the TSV export is unchanged).

**For the user's guide.** The SQL tab shows the statement exactly as run, with the user's criteria values filled in. It can be copied or saved and run in DB Browser for SQLite. Table aliases appear as t1, t2… (the gray label under each box's name), not the box names.

## QBE-4: Joins on more than one pair of fields

**Back end.** JoinSpec has a new optional field, AndOn []JoinColPair (JSON and_on), holding pairs after the first. left_col/right_col remain the first pair, so single-pair payloads are unchanged. ValidateGridState checks each extra pair against the schema whitelist, and now also checks that right_alias equals the table's own alias (always true for payloads from the page). buildFromClause writes each extra pair as AND left.col = right.col in the same ON clause:

LEFT JOIN "SOCIAL_INSTITUTION_CODES" AS "t3"

ON "t2"."c_inst_name_code" = "t3"."c_inst_name_code" AND "t2"."c_inst_code" = "t3"."c_inst_code"

**Front end.**

- A join is now stored as {leftAlias, rightAlias, kind, pairs: [{leftField, rightField}]}.
- The modal draws one row of drop-downs per pair (renderJoinPairs()). Rows after the first are labelled "And" and have a ✕. **+ Add fields** adds a row. Duplicate pairs are dropped on Set/Update Join. Cancel leaves an existing join unchanged.
- The line label shows the number of pairs when there is more than one, e.g. INNER JOIN (2 fields).
- buildTablesPayload() swaps both sides of every pair when the join was drawn in the opposite direction to the query's table order.
- **Shift-clicking two tables that are already joined now opens that join for editing**, instead of creating a second join between them. A second join between the same two tables was silently ignored by buildTablesPayload().
- Removing a table closes the join modal if it was open on that table.

**For the user's guide.** Tables whose keys span two fields (for example, social institutions: c_inst_name_code + c_inst_code) need both pairs in one join. Shift-click the two headers, choose the first pair, click **+ Add fields**, choose the second pair.

## QBE-5: Criteria of "Nan", "Inf" or "Infinity"

**Cause.** bindArg binds an operand as a number when strconv.ParseFloat accepts it. ParseFloat also accepts NaN, Inf and Infinity in any case. So Nan (a common pinyin name) was bound as a float NaN, which SQLite stores as NULL, and the comparison matched nothing.

**Fix.** bindArg rejects NaN and Inf results, so these operands are bound as text.

## Open items

- **Joins that close a loop.** With three or more tables joined in a cycle (A–B, B–C, C–A), buildTablesPayload() uses only the joins on its breadth-first path and silently ignores the one that closes the loop. Either warn the user or add the extra join's pairs as AND conditions on a later table.
- **Deleting a join.** A join can be edited but not deleted without removing one of its tables. Consider a **Delete Join** button in the modal's edit mode.
